title: Aizuwakamatsu — 会津若松
goal: Give a simple name and identify family relationships in context.

cards.title: A Familiar 会 in a Longer Name

blocks.text: Aizuwakamatsu is associated with Tsuruga Castle and historical castle-town culture. We will use a fictional family photograph, not require the learner to remember clans or dates.
**会津若松で家族の写真を見ました。** あいづわかまつで かぞくの しゃしんを みました。 — I looked at a family photograph in Aizuwakamatsu.

**家族 / かぞく — family**, assisted whole word; 族 remains encounter. We can identify the people with basic relationship vocabulary and read the complete location name with help. 会 already has a useful meeting verb from Hanamaki.

items: **Character:** 会 · **Orientation meaning/reading:** meet; 会う = あう; カイ; あい here · **Radical/components:** 人, ひと; modern upper 人-like shape over 云-like section · **Role:** Formal review; do not derive modern meeting grammar from the pieces.

**Character:** 津 · **Orientation meaning/reading:** harbour; つ, シン; づ here · **Radical/components:** 水 in 氵/さんずい form + 聿, historical sound element · **Role:** Encounter. The name's づ is learned in あいづ.

**Character:** 若 · **Orientation meaning/reading:** young; 若い = わかい; ジャク · **Radical/components:** 艹, くさかんむり, above a modern 右-like section · **Role:** Encounter. Its indexing grass top is not proof that “young” means grass.
**Character:** 松 · **Orientation meaning/reading:** pine; まつ, ショウ · **Radical/components:** 木, きへん + 公, historical sound element · **Role:** Encounter review from 松島.

blocks.text: Whole name: **あいづわかまつ**. Spell 会津, not **あいつ** or a guessed **かいつ** reading. Repeated characters help recognition without requiring all four to become new core assignments.

**名前 / なまえ — name; 名 / な — name in the taught compound.** 名 is indexed under **口**, くち, below **夕**. These shapes aid recognition; a modern evening/mouth mnemonic is not a universal explanation of naming.
**私の名前はゆきです。** わたしの なまえは ゆきです。 — My name is Yuki.

ゆき is a fictional person's name written in kana, not the snow noun 雪 here. 名前 combines 名 with 前 from Hirosaki. 前 does not necessarily mean a physical front in every compound. Learn the familiar whole word なまえ rather than translate “name-front.”
**お名前は何ですか。** おなまえは なんですか。 — What is your name?
**名前はゆきです。** なまえは ゆきです。 — My name is Yuki.

お is a polite prefix in the question. A direct name question should fit a suitable introduction context, rather than be the only way to begin every conversation. **私はゆきです。** わたしは ゆきです。 — I am Yuki, is also a simple introduction.
We omit the written kanji of a person's name because its intended reading has not been taught. Kana avoids pretending that every proper name can be read from a generic kanji rule.

cards.title: 父: My Father in This Context

blocks.text: **父 / ちち — father, commonly one's own father when speaking to someone outside the family; 父親 / ちちおや — father/parent**, assisted 親.

父 is its own radical, ちち. Recognise the whole form, with upper separated strokes and lower crossing strokes; it is not the same shape as 文. The historical parent/tool image is not a rule about current family roles.
**これは私の父です。** これは わたしの ちちです。 — This is my father.
**お父さん / おとうさん — father/dad**, a polite/familiar term used for someone else's father or in appropriate family address. Its reading is a whole word, not **おちちさん**.
**母 / はは — mother, commonly one's own mother in an outside-family description; 母親 / ははおや — mother/parent**, assisted 親.
母 is indexed in the **毋/母 family**, はは. Its inner marks help distinguish it from related modern forms such as 毎. Learn the whole mother word; the radical family does not make 毎日 mean “mother day.”
**これは私の母です。** これは わたしの ははです。 — This is my mother.

**お母さん / おかあさん — mother/mum**, appropriate as a polite/familiar family term. Notice the long **かあ** vowel. 父/母 and お父さん/お母さん have social/contextual uses, not one universal replacement rule for every family conversation.

**子ども / こども — child; 子 / こ — child in common words.** 子 is its own radical, こ. Its whole child-derived form connects back to 字's lower part. The top, outstretched middle and lower hook are recognition features, not separate word meanings added together.
**子どもがいます。** こどもが います。 — There is a child / someone has a child, depending on context.
**この子どもはゆきです。** この こどもは ゆきです。 — This child is Yuki.
We use 子ども as the ordinary taught spelling. 男の子/女の子 are useful later expansions when 男/女 become formal study; we do not silently introduce those extra assignments here.

cards.title: Relationships with の and と

blocks.text: **父と母 / ちちとはは — father and mother.**
**父と母はこの町に住んでいます。** ちちと ははは この まちに すんでいます。 — My father and mother live in this town.

**私の父 / わたしのちち — my father; 友だちのお母さん / ともだちのおかあさん — my friend's mother.** の links the relationship chain. と joins the two people in the topic; it differs from companion と in **母と行きます**, I go with my mother.
The family is fictional. We do not assume every learner has the same family composition; the picture and sentence identify the intended relationships for each exercise.
**写真に三人います。** しゃしんに さんにん います。 — There are three people in the photograph.
**父と母と子どもです。** ちちと ははと こどもです。 — They are a father, a mother and a child.

The people counter is **三人 / さんにん**. **三つ / みっつ** counts general items instead. An image of people can be described using the usual person-presence wording; the exercise explicitly describes the picture's people, not claims real people physically live inside the photograph.
一人/二人 are still ひとり/ふたり. Adding family vocabulary does not remove the irregular person-count forms already studied.
**母と会津若松に行きました。父は来ませんでした。** ははと あいづわかまつに いきました。ちちは きませんでした。 — I went to Aizuwakamatsu with my mother. My father did not come.
**子どもは白い鳥を見ました。** こどもは しろい とりを みました。 — The child saw a white bird.

The first と marks the companion; the negative past 来ませんでした is reviewed from Sendai. The last sentence adds a previously taught nature noun. A cultural city introduction does not constrain every practice action to a famous landmark; language can describe a simple invented visit.

items: Read 会津若松 and 名前. **Answer:** あいづわかまつ; なまえ.
Read 父 and 母 in one's own-family description. **Answer:** ちち; はは.
Read お父さん and お母さん. **Answer:** おとうさん; おかあさん.
What radical connects 子 with 字? **Answer:** 子.
Count three people. **Answer:** 三人 / さんにん.
In 母と行きます, what does と mark? **Answer:** the mother as companion, rather than an object bought.

blocks.text: 会津若松 is あいづわかまつ. 名前 is なまえ; 前's meaning in the compound is not a literal place description. 父/母 are ちち/はは in our own-family report. お父さん/お母さん are おとうさん/おかあさん in appropriate polite/familiar uses. 子ども is child. Use the person counter for a stated number of people.
**Recall task:** “I went with my mother. My father did not come.” **Model:** 母と行きました。父は来ませんでした。 Continue to Koriyama and identify learning roles.
